claim: Heavy fermions/scalars Q charged under the SM and a new confining SU(N)_IC with no light IC flavours (m_Q >> Lambda) cannot break their IC flux tube; the pair oscillates as a classical string system. For colour-neutral, EW-charged quirks in the mesoscopic/intermediate regime (oscillation amplitude ~0.1-10 cm, roughly 100 eV <~ Lambda <~ 10-30 keV for m_Q ~ 0.1-1 TeV) standard helix tracking fails, leaving a gap between HSCP/OoT reinterpretations (low Lambda) and monojet/single-track (high Lambda). The target: an ATLAS/CMS central-tracker coplanar/non-helical hit search above the FASER reach (179 GeV at Lambda=10 keV).
framework: Vector-like Q in (1,1,-1,N_IC) (or other SM reps) x SU(N_IC); Nambu-Goto string with massive endpoints, S = -m_Q sum int d tau_i - Lambda^2 int dA + S_ext (1708.02243 Eq.2); production via Drell-Yan; IC glueballs (m ~ 6 Lambda) the only IC hadrons.
assumptions: No IC-charged state lighter than Lambda (else strings break: hadronisation instead of quirks)
Lambda^2 >> external forces (Lorentz force, ionisation ~ (100 eV)^2) so that the pair's motion is planar (central force, angular momentum conserved)
Quirk is stable on detector timescales (lightest IC-charged state; no SM decay)
IC glueball emission per crossing is small/parameterised (eps = 0.1 used by FASER and Evans-Luty; Knapen et al. argue irrelevantly small at large separation)
Low cosmological reheat temperature T_RH <~ O(100 GeV) (required by 2512.20696 for the whole collider-accessible quirky region)
controlling_parameters: SM quantum numbers (charge, colour, SU(2) rep), spin
boost distribution / ISR (sets lab oscillation length d ~ 2 cm (gamma-1)(m_Q/100 GeV)(keV/Lambda)^2)
robust_predictions: Drell-Yan EW production cross section (FASER quotes 2-4% scale+PDF uncertainty)
Coplanarity of all hits of the pair (kinematic consequence of central force; holds for any central force much stronger than external ones)
Characteristic oscillation scale d_cm ~ 2 cm (gamma-1)(m_Q/100 GeV)(1 keV/Lambda)^2 setting which regime (two tracks / non-helical / single straight HIP-like track)
Slow (beta < 1) pairs with ~2x MIP charge; no annihilation for macroscopic strings (Kang-Luty Sec.4)
model_dependent_predictions: Annihilation location/timing and stopped-quirk rates (depend on unknown eps and stopped-bound-state energy loss; Evans-Luty call this highly uncertain)
Trigger efficiency (MET from ISR; eps_trig ~0.10 for DY at m_Q=800 GeV in 1708.02243 Tab.I)
Soft pion/glueball emission and SUEP-like patterns (microscopic, colored, Lambda >~ 10 GeV regime only; E_frac 0.2-1 ad hoc in 2506.11192)
W gamma/WZ quirkonium resonances + displaced glueball decay (GeV-scale Lambda natural squirks, 2504.02940)

constraints_checked.constraint: FASER direct search 186 fb^-1, (1,1,-1,N_IC=2): m_Q > 179 GeV at Lambda=10 keV; covers 300 eV < Lambda < 100 keV
constraints_checked.verdict: excludes only m_Q <~ 180 GeV; region above survives

constraints_checked.constraint: HSCP/monojet reinterpretation (12.9 fb^-1): uncoloured (1,1)_-1 fermion N_c=2 limits 650 GeV (Lambda=1 eV), 150 GeV (100 eV), none at 1 keV
constraints_checked.verdict: intermediate Lambda ~ keV essentially unconstrained for EW quirks at that luminosity; full Run-2 reinterpretation UNVERIFIED

constraints_checked.constraint: D0 quirk search m_Q >~ 120 GeV for 10 nm <~ l <~ 100 um

constraints_checked.verdict: covers part of parameter space; depends on eps; does not close target region (per FASER Fig.5 grey areas)

constraints_checked.constraint: Cosmology: glueball freeze-in -> BBN/CMB/gamma-ray/SIDM/Delta N_eff bounds require T_RH <~ O(100 GeV) throughout quirky collider region
constraints_checked.verdict: does not exclude collider region; imposes low-reheat cosmology (tension with standard baryogenesis)

constraints_checked.constraint: EW precision (rho/T) for split SU(2) doublet squirks: Delta < 43 GeV at 95% CL
constraints_checked.verdict: irrelevant for SU(2)-singlet benchmark; mild for doublets

constraints_checked.source_id: arXiv:1708.02243 Sec.II; arXiv:0805.4642 Sec.4.3; own estimate e v B(2T) ~ (11 eV)^2
constraints_checked.verdict: planarity holds for Lambda >~ 100 eV; degrades near 100 eV (ionisation ~ (100 eV)^2)

theory_uncertainties: eps (glueball emission per crossing) is not computable; affects stopping/annihilation, FASER survival and timing, minor for central tracks
Lab oscillation length depends on ISR/pT of the pair and opening angle (event-by-event); acceptance depends on Pythia ISR modelling (FASER 25% from shower-scale variation)
keV-scale Lambda is not predicted by neutral naturalness (folded SUSY/twin-type models give GeV-scale Lambda); it is 'natural' only in the log-flat sense of Kang-Luty Eq.1.2

For 30-100 keV the pair is a single straight HIP-like track with event-by-event variable invariant mass: coplanar-hit method does not apply there (1708.02243 Sec.I), so the target's quoted 0.1-100 keV range mixes two signatures
distinctiveness: Very high: no SM object produces two coplanar, non-helical, mutually-attracting slow tracks with ~2x ionisation; backgrounds are pile-up hit coincidences and conversions, argued removable (1708.02243 Sec.III). Neighbouring BSM (HSCP, R-hadrons, monopoles, multi-charged) give helical or straight tracks.
caveats: Target is not new as a proposal: coplanar-hit method (1708.02243, 300 fb^-1, <mu>=50, background assumed negligible, EW quirks to ~650 GeV) and GNN quirk tracking (2410.00269, m_Q <~ 700 GeV for 100 eV < Lambda < 5 keV, pile-up not studied) exist; status proposed-not-searched / theory-explored-untested at ATLAS/CMS. HL-LHC 200-PU performance and trigger path are the real open questions. Secondary targets (2506.11192, 2504.02940) belong to different (GeV-scale Lambda) regimes. Newer ATLAS/CMS HSCP recasts not checked (UNVERIFIED).
